Taking Cognizance And Issue Of Process Dated
18.05.2019 In Criminal Case No.2705/2019 (Arising Out
Of The Raghavendra Nagar Police Station, In Crime
No.14/2016) By The Honourable Ii Addl. Civil Judge
(Jr.Dn) And Jmfc Court At Kalaburagi For The
Offences Punishable U/Sec. 406, 465, 468, 471, 409, 420
R/W Sec. 34 Of Ipc Pursuant To The Chargesheet
Filed By The Respondent No.1.
 This Petition Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order
1.
The respondent-police after investigation laid the charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 465, 468, 471, 409 and 420 R/w Section 34 of IPC.

The summary of the charge sheet is that, the petitioner-accused No.2 herein along with the other accused, who, when working in the Department of Social Welfare, Karnataka, misused the funds released by the Government and disbursed it to various organizations without approval by the competent authorities.
2. The learned Magistrate, after accepting the charge sheet, took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons.

Sri R.S. Lagali, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that on similar set of charges, the Government had initiated departmental enquiry, and the enquiry officer after conducting a detailed enquiry, submitted a report stating that the charge against the petitioner herein are not proved.
The enquiry report submitted by the Retired District Judge was accepted by the Government vide order dated 24.06.2019 and the same has attained finality.
Hence, he submits that the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

In support, he place reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ashoo Surendranath Tewari vs. Deputy Superintendent of Police, EOW, CBI and another reported in (2020) 9 SCC 636 and the decision of the Co-ordinate Bhimanna S/O Mahadevappa Meti vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112286890/
2 Bench of this Court in the case of Mr. A.L.Jayaramu vs. State of Karnataka and others (Writ Petition No.19700/2018, D.D.27.07.2021).

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State submits that, merely because the petitioner has been exonerated in the departmental enquiry, it would not lead to exoneration or acquittal in criminal cases.

In support, he places reliance on the decision of the Honble Supreme Court in the case of State (NCT of Delhi) vs. Ajay Kumar Tyagi reported in 2012 (9) SCC 685.
5.

entities.text: State (NCT of Delhi) vs. Ajay Kumar Tyagi reported in 2012 (9) SCC 685
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
Admittedly, against the similar set of charges, departmental enquiry was initiated against the petitioner- accused No.2.

The charge against accused No.2 was that, he, when working as First Division Assistant under accused No.1 in the Social Welfare Department, in connivance with the other accused had misused the Government fund and disbursed it to Smt. Sumitradevi Mahila Mandali unauthorisedly.
7. The Retired District Judge after conducting an enquiry, submitted a report stating that the charges against the petitioner herein have not been proved.

On realising that the amounts were wrongly disbursed, the Mahila Mandali in question has returned the amount to the Government and there is no material to substantiate that the petitioner-accused No.2 was benefited from the amount disbursed to Mahila Mandali.

The Government vide order dated 24.06.2019 accepted the enquiry report submitted by the enquiry officer and exonerated the petitioner herein of the charges leveled against him and the same has attained finality.

8. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Radheshyam Kejriwal Vs. State of West Bengal (2011) 3 SCC 581 has laid the principle which reads thus:
"38.

entities.text: Radheshyam Kejriwal Vs. State of West Bengal (2011) 3 SCC 581
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mahadevappa Meti vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (v) Adjudication proceedings by the Enforcement Directorate is not prosecution by a competent court of law to attract the provisions of Article 20(2) of the Constitution or Section 300 of the Code of Criminal Procedure;
(vi) The finding in the adjudication proceedings in favour of the person facing trial for identical violation will depend upon the nature of finding.

If the exoneration in adjudication proceedings is on technical ground and not on merit, prosecution may continue; and (vii) In case of exoneration, however, on merits where the allegation is found to be not sustainable at all and the person held innocent, criminal prosecution on the same set of facts and circumstances cannot be allowed to continue, the underlying principle being the higher standard of proof in criminal cases."
9.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court consisting of three learned Judges in the case of the State (NCT of Delhi) (supra) without reference to the decision in the case of Radheshyam Kejriwal (supra) has held that the High Court misread the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1228 judgment in P S Rajya -vs- State of Bihar ((1996) 9 SCC 1) and exoneration in departmental proceeding ipso facto would not lead to exoneration or acquittal in a criminal case.

entities.text: P S Rajya -vs- State of Bihar ((1996) 9 SCC 1)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further noted that the decision of P S Rajya case which was rendered by the Bench consisting of two learned Judge was distinguished in a subsequent decision in the case of State -vs- L. Krishnamohan which was again by a two Judges and accordingly held that the decision in P S Rajya was not an authority for the presumption that exoneration in departmental proceeding ipso facto would lead to a judgment of acquittal in a criminal trial.

10. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Hyder Consulting (UK) Ltd. v. State of Orissa, (2015) 2 SCC 189 has held that a decision can be said to be given per incuriam when the court of record has acted in ignorance of any previous decision of its own, or a subordinate court has acted in ignorance of a decision of the court of record.

entities.text: Hyder Consulting (UK) Ltd. v. State of Orissa, (2015) 2 SCC 189
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore the decision of State (NCT of Delhi) which has not taken into account and consideration of the earlier decision of the Supreme Court in Radheshyam is said to be per incuriam.

11. The Full Bench of this Court in the case of Govindanaik G Kalaghatigi -vs- West Patent Press Co.
Ltd.

entities.text:
Govindanaik G Kalaghatigi -vs- West Patent Press Co.
Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has held that where there is a conflict between two decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of the same Bench strength, it is latter of the decision that would prevail.

The decision of the Bench consisting of three Judges in the case of Ashoo Surendranath Tiwari would prevail over the decision in the case of State (NCT NC: 2023:KHC-K:1228 of Delhi) rendered by consisting of three Judges which is a latter judgment.

Though the decision of the State (NCT of Delhi) was unanimous and whereas in the case of Radheshyam Kejriwal it was a majority of 2:1, the total strength of the Bench that they decided the case is deemed to be the Bench strength of that decision despite dissenting opinion as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shanti Fragrances - vs- Union of India (2018) 11 SCC 305.
12.

entities.text: Shanti Fragrances - vs- Union of India (2018) 11 SCC 305
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the departmental enquiry was initiated against the petitioner-accused No.2 and after conducting the enquiry, the Enquiry Officer submitted a report stating that the charges against the delinquent have not been proved.

Hence, in view of the ratio enunciated by the Hon'ble Bhimanna S/O Mahadevappa Meti vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112286890/
4

entities.text: Mahadevappa Meti vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apex Court, the impugned criminal proceeding cannot be continued against the accused, who has been exonerated on identical charges in the departmental enquiry, the underlying principle being higher standard of proof in criminal cases.

13. In view of the aforesaid, I am of the considered view that the petitioner having been exonerated in the departmental enquiry on merits, it would be an abuse of process of law to continue the criminal proceedings against the petitioner, since the probability of conviction of the petitioner is remote and bleak.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1228 ii. The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.2705/2019, pending on the file of II Addl.
Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC Court, Kalaburagi, insofar as it relates to the petitioner - accused No.2 is hereby quashed.
